{{Quote|We rule the Sith. Here we will build a sovereignty of the dark side to overcome millennia of injustice. But I am the rightful ruler, for I alone possess the curiosity to translate their secrets and apply them to larger patterns of conquest. I foresee what will become a magnificent Sith Empire.|Sorzus Syn, Dark Lord of the Sith|<ref name="BoS" />}}
The '''Sith Empire''', later known as the '''Old Sith Empire''' or '''Original Sith Empire''', was a wealthy and powerful empire in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] established by [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] who were [[Exiles|banished]] from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] after their defeat at the [[Battle of Corbos]] at the end of the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]].

The [[Exiles|Jedi Exiles]] [[Discovery of Korriban|discovered]] the remote [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], where they encountered the native [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith species]], who worshipped the [[The Force|Force]]-wielding newcomers as gods. The Dark Jedi came to rule and even interbreed with the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] natives, and began a long period of building and expansion as they reorganized into the [[Sith/Legends|Sith Order]]. As the Sith Lords' knowledge of the [[Dark side of the Force|Dark Side]] grew, so did their power, and over many generations, the empire expanded from Korriban to encompass many star systems. The Sith Empire developed in complete isolation within the [[Stygian Caldera]] for two thousand [[Galactic Standard Calendar|years]] before it eventually rediscovered the Republic.

Under the leadership of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]], the Empire invaded Republic space during the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]], but it suffered a devastating defeat. The Sith Empire was believed to have been destroyed by Republic forces at the end of the [[Post–Great Hyperspace War counterinvasion]] of the Sith Empire. However, the Sith Lord [[Tenebrae|Vitiate]] survived the destruction and [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|rebuilt the Sith Empire]] in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]].

With a legacy that extended across [[Time/Legends|millennia]], the Sith would create [[Sith Empire (Exar Kun)/Legends|numerous]] [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|different]] [[New Sith|iterations]] of the Sith Empire and later [[Grand Plan/Legends|acquired]] [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] control by the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], with the Sith Lord [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] [[Declaration of a New Order|transforming]] the Republic into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|First Galactic Empire]]. After Sidious' death, his Empire would [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|diminish]] in size and eventually evolve into a [[Fel Empire|new regime]] without Sith leadership, until the machinations of [[Darth Krayt]] would see it reorganize into a [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|brand new Sith Empire]].

==History==
===Origin===
{{Quote|Once we were mighty Jedi of the Republic, brothers in the Force. But the Great Schism between the Dark side and the Light turned Jedi against Jedi. Our ancestors were defeated, driven off, cast out! But we turned our exile into victory, here on the far side of the galaxy. In these unblemished worlds we found the Sith people treated us as Gods! After many centuries some of us have interbred with the Sith while others still bear true Jedi blood. Our Sith Empire is great, rich, and powerful. This is our Golden Age.|[[Marka Ragnos]], [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]]|<ref name="TOTJ 2" />
}}
[[File:XoxaanMuur.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[Karness Muur]] and [[XoXaan]] lead the Exiles onto Korriban.]]
The [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] civilization began around the [[Galactic Standard Calendar|year]] [[100,000 BBY/Legends|100,000 BBY]], by which time a species of [[Color/Legends|red]] skinned humanoids had evolved on the planet Korriban.<ref name="JvSTEGF">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> They lived a barbaric, yet strangely harmonious, existence filled with constant warring between the various divided nations on their world.<ref name="END" /> During their pre-industrial age, by [[30,000 BBY]], the inhabitants of Korriban fought off an [[Incursion of Korriban|incursion]] from the [[Killik/Legends|Killiks]].<ref name="TEA" /> It was under the iron rule of [[King/Legends|King]] [[Adas]] that the Sith first became unified. He was declared the [[Sith'ari/Legends|Sith'ari]]: the ultimate being.<ref name="END" /> It was he who first formed a [[Sith Empire (Pre-Republic)|Sith Empire]] around the year [[28,000 BBY]], and his reign lasted for three [[Time/Legends|centuries]].<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide" />

The relative stability of this empire was first challenged in [[27,700 BBY]] when the Sith were visited by the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]].<ref name="JvSTEGF" /> These aliens from the distant [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] attempted to lull the ancient Sith King into their confidence by providing him with the knowledge to create [[Holocron/Legends|Holocrons]]. However, their true motive of conquest quickly became apparent. This led to King Adas bringing the full might of the Sith Empire to bear on the Rakata, and although he succeeded in driving them away from Korriban, it came at the cost of his own life.<ref name="END" />

Using the remains of the enemy craft, the once-primitive Sith were propelled into a space age and were armed with the power of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. Using these newly-acquired tools from the Infinite Empire, the Sith Empire conquered other nearby worlds—which became part of Sith Space—and relocated their capital from ancient Korriban to the neighboring world of [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]].<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide" /> The reign of this empire was shortlived, however, as it dissolved into [[Korriban civil war|civil war]] after the death of King Adas, leaving his people to regress into a more primitive state.<ref name="END" /> A [[Kissai heretics|group of Sith priests]] of the [[Kissai]] caste interpreted the death of Adas as a sign to reject the dark side-dominated beliefs of their people. Labeled as heretics for their actions, these Sith were banished and settled on the planet [[Tund/Legends|Tund]], where they became the [[Sorcerers of Tund/Legends|Sorcerers of Tund]].<ref name="KotORWE5">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/KOTORweben5|text=KOTOR Campaign Guide Web Enhancement 5: Karnak Tetsu, Sorcerer of Tund}}</ref> A number of Sith also established a [[library-temple]] on the world of [[Krayiss II]] around [[14,000 BBY]] where they slumbered and their [[Force ghost/Legends|spirits]] continued to haunt the temple for the next 10,000 years.<ref name="ATDS">{{WEGCite|story=A Tale from the Dark Side|book=Tales of the Jedi Companion}}</ref>

Around the year [[7000 BBY]], [[Dathka Graush/Legends|Dathka Graush]] initiated a [[Korriban civil war (Dathka Graush)|civil war]] that left most of the cities of Korriban in ruin.<ref name="TEA" /> The planet [[Arkania/Legends|Arkania]] also fell under the dominion of the Sith, and by 7000 BBY, they had established a library known as [[Veeshas Tuwan]] on it.<ref name="EGAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref>

Around the year [[6900 BBY]], [[Exiles|exiled Dark Jedi]] who were defeated in the [[Battle of Corbos]], which concluded the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]], landed on Korriban, a desolate world inhabited by the relatively primitive but unusually [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith species]].<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide" /> Upon arriving, the Dark Jedi attempted to subjugate the Sith and take whatever knowledge they possessed. The Sith attempted to protect their secrets, but fell to the superior training and technology of the invaders.<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> Using their training in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], the fallen Jedi amazed the Sith and elevated themselves to god-like status, becoming the rulers of the Sith people. Over the next two thousand years, interbreeding occurred between the fallen Jedi and the Sith by means of [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]], which led to the term ''"Sith"'' being used to identify not only the original inhabitants of Korriban, but also their fallen Jedi masters.<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide" /> This intermingling between the two species continued across hundreds of generations, and the hybridized offspring of this union became the new ruling class of the Sith.<ref name="TOR" /> Thus, the Sith Empire was born.<ref name="JvSTEGF" />

Once the Exiles became Sith Lords, an overly ambitious group of them decided to retrace their steps back to the Republic using a navicomputer from one of the ships that brought them to Sith Space. Despite the objections of Ajunta Pall, these Sith Lords decided to embark on their quest back to the Republic and [[First battle between Jedi and Sith|wage war against the Jedi]]. While the greater Sith were unaware of their fate, this expedition did succeed in their goal and fought against the Jedi Order. However, they were defeated and alerted the Jedi that the Exiles had claimed a world of their own. Despite this discovery, the Jedi were unable to determine where Sith Space was and could not locate the growing Sith Empire.<ref name="JvSTEGF" />

===The Golden Age of the Sith===
In time, the Sith formed an immensely rich and powerful empire, built upon the use of sorcery and the dark side which fueled their technology.<ref name="TOTJ 2" /> At its height, the Sith Empire ruled over at least 120 worlds.<ref name="JvSTEGF" /> Long before reaching their Golden Age, the Sith Empire fought in the [[Battle of Kalsunor]], where [[Silooth/Legends|Silooths]] were first used in order to subjugate the planet [[Kalsunor]], which had long resisted conquest. After the world was defeated, the army of Silooths were left behind on that world, where they remained for years.<ref name="DSS">''[[The Dark Side Sourcebook]]''</ref>

Over the centuries that followed, the two civilizations thrived in isolation.<ref name="TOTJ 2" /> To the galaxy outside their space, the Sith Empire was considered nothing more than a myth.<ref name="TOTJ 4">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 4]]</ref>

[[File:Chhodos-TFotSE2.jpg|thumb|The Sith Empire at its zenith]]
Though the [[Stygian Caldera]] that surrounded their territory confined them to Sith Space, it also meant that few travelers stumbled on their empire. However, on occasion, ships that braved the Caldera were captured by the Sith, becoming slaves
to ranking nobles in the empire. After generations, these slaves slowly forgot their origins and largely identified themselves as being Sith. It was through the entry of inhabitants from the [[Tapani sector/Legends|Tapani sector]] that led to the influx of highly-technical slaves that developed the Sith Empire's technological and medical base; millennia later, these Tapani humans formed the backbone of the [[Lost Tribe of Sith|Lost Tribe of the Sith]].<ref name="LotSPa">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Paragon]]''</ref> Also during this age, Sith holocrons spoke of the legendary [[Muur Talisman]] which many desired to find and possess.<ref name="KotORHB">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic Handbook]]''</ref> While the Sith Empire had grown into a powerful force, they now faced potential self-annihilation. Having starved for centuries, the Sith sought to expand and conquer new worlds and enemies to subjugate.<ref name="DSS" />

At some point during the Golden Age, the Sith Lord [[Ieldis]] created a slaver organization known as [[the Crucible]] which was tasked with capturing refugees displaced from war in order for them to be used as a slave army that would fight for the Sith Empire. The Crucible long outlived the empire it served.<ref name="KotORD">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic Volume 8: Destroyer]]''</ref>

[[File:Sadow_vs_Kressh.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Ragnos's death left a power struggle between Sadow and Kressh.]]
The late Golden Age saw relative stability. At the time, the Dark Lord of the Sith was a particularly powerful and long-lived individual named [[Marka Ragnos]]. Through his mastery of the dark side and his fierce intelligence, he had risen through the ranks in order to attain the position of Dark Lord. Ragnos would prove to be one of the last rulers of the original Sith Empire.<ref name="JvSTEGF" />

Ragnos often placed his rivals against one another, manipulated them into challenging him openly, or simply had them assassinated.<ref name="JvSTEGF" /> While many factions sought to expand beyond the confines of Sith Space, Ragnos forbade it, as he well remembered how his ancestors were defeated by the Jedi Order. He knew how powerful the Jedi were and he was not confident that the Sith Empire was strong enough to challenge them.<ref name="DSS" /> After ruling for a century, his [[Funeral of Marka Ragnos|death]] caused a power vacuum within the leadership of the Empire that saw the isolationist [[Ludo Kressh]] and the expansionist [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]] amass power in order to propel themselves onto the Sith throne.<ref name="JvSTEGF" />

===Great Hyperspace War===
[[File:InvasionFleet.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Naga Sadow invades the Galactic Republic.]]
{{Quote|Across the reaches of the galaxy, through seas of dark stars, rivers of whispering black shadow from the Republic's ancient past. Evil history we had thought forgotten.|Jedi Master Ooroo|<ref name="Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 1">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 1|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 1]]</ref>}}
In circa [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], the isolation of the Sith was broken when two young [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] explorers called [[Gav Daragon|Gav]] and [[Jori Daragon]] accidentally stumbled upon Korriban whilst they attempted to establish a [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] in an effort to expand their trade options. However, the feuding Sith had little interest in peaceful trade with the Republic, instead capturing the pair as spies and imprisoning them on Ziost to await interrogation. By this point in their history, the Sith held little memory of the Republic, who lived in distant regions of space compared to them. This saw Ludo Kressh and his conservative allies claim that the two travelers were the precursors of an invasion of their territory, whilst his rival Naga Sadow held the view that the Republic offered new lands to conquer. In secret, Sadow also believed that focusing on conquest of the Republic would unite the strained factions of the Empire and distract the populace from the political problems they faced in their native territory. A tribunal of Sith rulers later sentenced the Daragons to death, but Sadow secretly had them rescued and sheltered at his own isolated fortress. However, he left behind evidence to suggest that the rescue attempt was done so by Republic agents and used this to galvanize the Sith Council by exploiting their fears and doubts. The Daragons proved to be the perfect scapegoats for Sadow, who convinced comrades that an invasion was imminent and that they needed to conduct a preemptive attack against their enemy.<ref name="NEC" />

Whilst the Daragons were kept at his fortress world, Ludo Kressh began to uncover signs that Sadow was responsible for freeing the two alien intruders. Thus, he gathered [[Ludo Kressh's faction|forces loyal]] to him in order to assault Naga Sadow's domain and expose him as a traitor. This was partly also an attempt by Kressh to take the mantle of leadership of the Sith Empire. However, this all fell into Sadow's plan, as he was well-prepared for his rival's ''"surprise attack".'' In the resultant chaos, he convinced Jori Daragon to abandon her brother in order to escape into Republic space. Intending to warn the Galactic Republic of the dangerous Sith Empire, she fled in ''[[Starbreaker 12]],'' at which point Sadow unleashed his own hidden forces, annihilating Kressh's own; this included Kressh's flagship, seemingly taking him with it. In the aftermath, Naga Sadow declared himself as the new Dark Lord of the Sith and revealed that he had secretly placed a transmitter on Jori Daragon's vessel, allowing the Empire to trace her journey into Republic territory. After consolidating his forces, Sadow gathered his armies of bloodthirsty Massassi warriors in preparation for the upcoming invasion.<ref name="NEC" /> Despite the little intelligence he had of his enemy, the Sith Empire's vast invasion force moved through the [[Daragon Trail]] into Republic space.<ref name="TEA" /> Alongside the Dark Lord was his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] Gav Daragon. They sent their armada to follow his sister's tracking beacon, leading to the surprise Sith onslaught starting at the [[Empress Teta system/Legends|Koros Major system]].<ref name="NEC" />

The Dark Lord was well-aware that his forces would be insufficient in combatting the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] but made use of the element of surprise to aid him, and, for a time, it worked. The Koros system fell to the Sith's might and the Empire's naval forces spread through the [[Koros Trunk Line/Legends|Koros Trunk Line]] to assault the [[Foerost Shipyards|shipyards]] at [[Foerost/Legends|Foerost]], whereupon the Sith moved to assault [[Kaikielius/Legends|Kaikielius]], [[Metellos/Legends|Metellos]], [[Basilisk]], [[Shawken]] and ultimately [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] itself. The Sith armies on Coruscant managed to march across the [[Senate District/Legends|Legislative District]] and onto the steps of the [[Senate Hall]], where they were fought off by the defending Jedi forces.<ref name="TEA" /> At [[Empress Teta/Legends|Koros Major]], the Sith proved relentless and unpredictable in their attacks, which was necessary due to Sadow's limited knowledge of the region of space, which led to the Republic not faring well in this conflict, which became known as the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]].<ref name="NEC" /> Unknown to the Republic, Sadow had stationed his [[Sith Meditation Sphere]] around [[Primus Goluud/Legends|Primus Goluud]], where he employed Sith sorcery to create illusionary phantoms that made the Empire's enemies believe that the Sith had far greater numbers.<ref name="TEA" />

At some point during the conflict, Sadow dispatched some of his forces to locate [[Lignan crystal]]s, which were to be used in the creation of advanced lightsabers for use against the Republic and the Jedi. One of the ships dispatched was the ''[[Omen]].'' However, it crashed on the primitive world of [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]]. While the crew at first attempted to return to space, they were unable, and later adapted to life on the planet amongst the native [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]].<ref name="LotSPr">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Precipice]]''</ref> During the war, several Jedi were corrupted and joined the forces of the Sith Empire, one of whom was the [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]] [[Saes Rrogon]], who commanded the [[Harbinger (Sith dreadnaught)|''Harbinger'']].<ref name="C">''[[Crosscurrent]]''</ref> In the closing stages of the conflict, the newly-trained Sith [[Valik Kodank]] diverted resources for the construction of her own [[Temple of Pain|Sith Temple]] located in the [[Tascollan Nebula/Legends|Tascollan Nebula]]. She would later leave the Sith Empire with a sect consisting of her followers in order to continue their existence elsewhere.<ref name="Light and Dark">"[[Light and Dark (adventure)|Light and Dark]]"</ref> As the conflict continued, it was known that the Jedi used the planet [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]] as a staging ground for raids into Sith territory.<ref name="TJC">''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]''</ref>

After learning of the Sith sorcery being used in the war, the Republic became emboldened to strike back against the Empire.<ref name="fall4">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 4]]</ref> This saw them being reinforced from the naval base at [[Anaxes/Legends|Anaxes]], which they used to push back the Sith armada to their beachhead at Koros Major.<ref name="TEA" /> Their combined forces pushed towards Primus Goluud, where they attacked the Empire's forces present in the region. By this point, Gav Daragon had turned against his [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Master]], but Sadow had tricked him into getting trapped on the Meditation Ship. He revealed to [[Teta/Legends|Empress Teta]] the hyperspace coordinates of the Sith Empire's territories. In an effort to destroy his enemies, Naga Sadow used his own Sith technology to cause the Primus Goluud star to erupt into a supernova, killing Daragon, whilst he made his escape back to Sith Space with what few forces he had left.<ref name="fall4" />

When Naga Sadow returned to the Sith Empire, he was greeted by an unexpected figure: his rival Ludo Kressh, who had not died in their earlier battle, but had been warned by his spies of the assassination attempt. Showing no mercy, Kressh's forces mercilessly attacked Sadow's battered fleet before they could recover. However, Sadow's forces fought with wild frenzy as they had nothing to lose, leading to both sides being devastated as a result at the [[second battle of Korriban]]. Kressh himself was killed when one of Sadow's battleships rammed into it, at which point the fleets of the Republic arrived and attacked the weakened Sith forces. The Republic forces decimated the remaining Sith fleets and brought about the downfall of their empire in the resultant crossfire. In a final desperate gamble, Sadow gathered what few followers he could and fled from the battlefield whilst being pursued by Republic ships. Utilizing Sith sorcery, he had his lone warship fly through the [[Denarii Nova]], causing solar flares that [[Battle at the Denarii Nova|destroyed]] his pursuers.<ref name="NEC" />

With Kressh dead and Sadow missing, [[Shar Dakhan]] became acting Dark Lord of the Sith. Sensing defeat and possible surrender being the only options available to them, he commanded his warriors to make suicidal attacks against the invading enemy fleets, but it was not enough to stop the Republic from winning.<ref name="TEA" /> Whilst the Sith by this point no longer posed a threat, [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Pultimo]] was still unsatisfied as to the outcome of the conflict. Thus, [[Post–Great Hyperspace War counterinvasion|Jedi and Republic forces were sent to Korriban as well as other Sith planets in order to ensure that no remnants of the Sith Empire remained]]. This act forced a number of Sith to flee into space, where they were led by a [[Tenebrae|Sith who had arisen]] to take Naga Sadow's place as the new Dark Lord. Members of this exile fleet later settled on Dromund Kaas, where they waited for centuries in order to get their revenge against the Republic.<ref name="TOR 12" /> One of the last holdouts was that of [[Elcho Kressh]], who spent years developing a counterattack plan outside the Caldera where he made most of the few forces available to him. Utilizing a tactic used by Naga Sadow, he began recruiting groups that were hostile to the Republic, which ranged from pirate bands to mercenary militias and other such species, which allowed him to build an impressive force. However, on the eve of his planned invasion, Elcho suffered from a ruptured stomach after heavy drinking, which killed him within hours, thus ending any plans of revenge.<ref name="KEn">[[Knight Errant (novel)|''Knight Errant'']]</ref>

The Sith Empire was broken as a result, though unknown to the Republic, Sadow had in fact escaped in the struggle. He fled to [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] in his single [[Derriphan-class battleship]], which was buried on the moon, while the Dark Lord's [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] created [[Massassi Temple|Temples]] for their master.<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide" /> One of the Sith Lords to die during the conflict was Lord [[Garu]], the holder of King Adas' holocron, who perished on the world of [[Ashas Ree/Legends|Ashas Ree]], thus leaving the ancient relic behind, where it remained undiscovered for centuries.<ref name="END" /> The Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic worked to destroy any remaining strongholds of the Sith, which saw the end of their once glorious empire. After their defeat, a group of Sith retreated to the planet [[Thule/Legends|Thule]], home to a stealth regiment where they worked alongside special forces in order to build up once more and set themselves up as an advance force for an eventual return of the empire. However, no one came, and the forces on Thule remained in the shadows for generations, waiting for their moment at getting their revenge.<ref name="GOR">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> Some Sith Lords disappeared on haunted worlds such as [[Vjun/Legends|Vjun]].<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Tfotse12.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A defeated Naga Sadow attempts to rebuild on Yavin 4.]]
Following the supposed destruction of the Sith Empire, the Jedi worked to destroy whatever remained of the Sith's legacy, which included talismans, temples, and holocrons. This was an attempt by the Jedi to prevent the dark knowledge of the Sith from being used by other dark side practitioners, or by students who could be influenced by those teachings. Among the many locations destroyed, the ancient Sith library on Arkania known as Veeshas Tuwan was destroyed by a group of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]].<ref name="TJC" /> [[Jedi Shadow]]s worked to destroy any dark side artifacts created by the Sith, such as [[Sith talisman/Legends|amulets]] and talismans. While the ranks of the Jedi Shadows destroyed most of these tainted artifacts, items such as holocrons were kept in the custody of the Jedi Order, though many others were left in the burial vaults of the Sith Lords.<ref name="JATM">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref> Any surviving manuscripts and books were later taken to the [[Galactic Museum/Legends|Galactic Museum]] at [[Galactic City/Legends|Republic City]], where they were stored in the Sith Hall for visitors to see.<ref name="TJC" /> Many of these artifacts were later taken by the secret Jedi cabal known as the [[Jedi Covenant]].<ref name="KotORV">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic: Vindication]]''</ref> Despite their efforts, many great Sith weapons would be forgotten and lost for ages, such as the dreaded [[Dark Reaper]].<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide" />

Though the Empire was destroyed, one of its legacies remained in the form of the Crucible, which continued to operate in the shadows for centuries, abducting countless people and turning them into ruthless warriors.<ref name="KotORD" /> One of the few known artifacts that were kept by the Jedi Order included the [[Holocron of Naga Sadow]], which was kept in order to provide insight into the origins of the ancient Sith. Ultimately, the campaigns of the Jedi to bury the teachings of the Sith was partly successful, with much of the Sith Empire's history being masked in shadows over the centuries that followed.<ref name="TJC" />

==Legacy==
{{Quote|You thought that the corrupted remnants of the Republic, the machines spawned by technology that Revan led into battle were the Sith? You are wrong. The Sith is a belief. And its empire, the true Sith Empire, rules elsewhere. And Revan knew the true war is not against the Republic. It waits for us, beyond the Outer Rim. And he has gone to fight it, in his own way.|[[Kreia]], to [[Meetra Surik]]|<ref name="KotOR2">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>}}
With the Sith Empire's devastating defeat in the Great Hyperspace War, its long reign came to an end. Worlds such as Korriban became lasting monuments that provided only traces of its splendor.<ref name="FFCA">{{JournalCite|14|From the Files of Corellia Antilles}}</ref> The planet Dromund Kaas itself also vanished for a time, until it was discovered by the Empire-in-Exile, led by the Sith Emperor, which had been rebuilding its forces within the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]. This faction of the Sith, along with other relics, continued to influence and shape events in the galaxy for thousands of years.<ref name="TOR" /> It was from that point onward that the term "Sith" became a title given to those that practiced the Sith teachings.<ref name="TJC" /> Among the many legacies of the ancient Sith were their various [[Sith Elite Warbot|warbots]], that were deactivated after the defeat of the Empire. These few battle droids remained hidden, with some emerging during various events such as the later [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]] and even during the [[Jedi Civil War]].<ref name="TotJ">''[[Threats of the Galaxy]]''</ref> It was believed that very few Sith starships survived the devastating conclusion of the Great Hyperspace War, though knowledge of their construction was believed to still reside within scrolls and holocrons. However, these vessels were inferior compared to designs that would be developed in the following years.<ref name="TSC">{{GamerCite|5|The Sith Compendium}}</ref>

The first of its kind, the ancient Sith Empire set the precedent for future Sith rule. Long after its fall, many Lords would seek to create their own dominions in the original empire's image. These efforts were met with varying success across the ages, but eventually resulted in the downfall of the [[Old Republic era|Old Republic]], and the rise of a galaxy-wide [[Galactic Empire|Empire]] whose power eclipsed that of its predecessor.<ref name="BoS" /> 

Other legacies of the ancient Sith included the manipulations of long-dead Sith Lords such as Marka Ragnos, with the [[Disciples of Ragnos]] forming during the era of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. This group sought to bring about the return of their master until they were defeated by [[Jaden Korr]].<ref name="JK:JA">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref> Decades after its creation, the Galactic Empire was destroyed, and it seemed that the legacy of the Sith Empire was gone with it. But, in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]], the dark history of the planet Dromund Kaas resurfaced, and in an effort to protect his fledgling [[New Jedi Order]], [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] worked with [[New Republic Intelligence Service|New Republic Intelligence]] to bury the knowledge of the world in order to ensure that its corruption would not bring further threats to the galaxy.<ref name="TDFS">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050407a|series=The Dark Forces Saga|text=Part 1}}</ref> However, unknown to many, a forgotten remnant of the Sith Empire had been left abandoned on the planet Kesh, which formed the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]], who sought to bring about the great splendors of their ancestors to the galaxy.<ref name="O">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Omen]]''</ref>

Even further into the future, the dark shadow of the Sith still fell across the galaxy when the teachings of [[XoXaan]], now a long-dead Sith spirit, were used by the fallen Jedi known as [[Darth Krayt]], who used them to found the [[One Sith]].<ref name="Legacy17">[[Legacy (2006) 17|''Legacy'' (2006) 17]]</ref> He later succeeded in taking control of the [[Fel Empire]] and made himself the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]], thus creating a new [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Sith Empire]].<ref name="LFAD1">[[Legacy (2006) 32|''Legacy'' (2006) 32]]</ref>

===Exar Kun's Sith Empire===
{{Main|Sith Empire (Exar Kun)/Legends}}
[[File:Exarkunsithholocron.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Exar Kun discovers a Sith Holocron.]]
{{Quote|I am here to warn you Jedi, you must not interfere with the work of the dark side. The Dark Lords of the Sith are destined to rise again. ''Nothing'' can prevent that.''"<br />"''You can't frighten us with useless prophecies. I thought Master Arca drove you away when he buried your bones on that barren moon.''"<br />"''Arca ''cannot'' interfere with the ''dead''&hellip;nor can he help ''you'', poor Jedi, to avoid your destiny.''"<br />"''What are you ''talking'' about?''"<br />"''You&hellip;will be one of the ''great ones''.|Freedon Nadd tells Ulic Qel-Droma of his destiny as a Sith Lord|audio=Nadd3-DLotS.flac|<ref name="Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio)">[[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|''Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith'' audio drama]]</ref>}}
In [[4400 BBY]], the fallen Jedi [[Freedon Nadd]] discovered two artifacts that the Jedi Shadows had failed to destroy. The first was [[Holocron of King Adas]] and the second, the [[Force ghost/Legends|spirit]] of Naga Sadow himself which Nadd used to absorb himself in the teachings of the Sith. After communing with the long dead Sith Lord,<ref name="JvSTEGF" /> Freedon Nadd destroyed Sadow's spirit<ref name="NEC" /> and then used his newly acquired power to conquer [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]]. Nadd's spirit remained on Onderon for centuries after his death.<ref name="JvSTEGF" />

In [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]], a young Jedi known as [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] became curious about the teachings of the Sith and was thus lured to the Dark Side by the ghost of Freedon Nadd. His actions led to the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], which tore the galaxy apart and instigated the fall of [[Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends|Ulic Qel-Droma]]. Kun recruited Qel-Droma as well as many Jedi into his [[Brotherhood of the Sith]]. Kun and Qel-Droma led their reborn [[Sith Empire (Exar Kun)/Legends|Sith Empire]] and caused great destruction during their short reign of power. One of the many Sith inspired cults that formed after the conflict was the [[Krath/Legends|Krath]], who had learned much of their power from Sith artifacts that survived the Great Hyperspace War. This group later allied with Exar Kun and Ulic Qel-Droma in the Great Sith War. It was the Krath who were responsible for uncovering the dreaded Sith weapon known as the Dark Reaper and used it during the conflict. The rule of this Sith Empire continued until Kun's [[Battle of Yavin 4 (Great Sith War)|defeat]] at Yavin 4 in [[3996 BBY]].<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide" />

===Revan and Malak's Sith Empire===
{{Main|Darth Revan's Sith Empire}}
[[File:DarthRevan_DarthMalak_EGF.png|thumb|right|150px|Revan and Malak returned from the Unknown Regions as Sith.]]
{{Quote|Three years ago, Revan and Malak returned at the head of a massive invasion fleet. Revan had assumed the title of Sith Lord; the hero had become a conqueror.|Dorak|<ref name="KOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
In [[3976 BBY]] the [[Mandalorian Wars]] engulfed the galaxy, threatening the destruction of the Galactic Republic. The [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] abstained from participating in the war, sensing danger, but not all Jedi followed their example. A Jedi known as [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] recruited [[Revanchist|like-minded members of the order]] and led the Republic to victory over the Mandalorians, ending the war in [[3960 BBY]].<ref name="KOTOR" /> Some time during or after the war, Revan visited the [[Trayus Academy]] on the Sith world of [[Malachor V]]. There, he discovered evidence that the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] survived the Great Hyperspace War and was hiding in the Unknown Regions. Revan and his apprentice, [[Darth Malak|Malak]], pursued these rumors<ref name="KotOR2" /> and information that [[Mandalore the Ultimate]] told Revan as he was dying, [[Mission to Dromund Kaas|leading them to]] [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]]. There, they came into contact with the Sith Emperor, who turned them to the dark side. Revan was sent back to the Republic to prepare it for the invasion of the Sith Empire, but instead Revan and Malak broke free of the Sith Emperor and, thinking the Sith Emperor's commands were their own desires, established their own Sith Empire.<ref name="Revan">''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]''</ref><ref name="Forums">{{TORweb|url=community/showthread.php?p=2133028#edit2133028|text=Daniel Erickson on the SWTOR.com forums}}</ref> Secretly, the pair searched for ancient [[Star Map]]s that led them to the [[Star Forge]], a treasure of the forgotten Rakatan Infinite Empire. Using the Star Forge, Revan raised his own Sith Empire and invaded the Galactic Republic.<ref name="KOTOR" />

As the Sith's conquest continued unchecked, worlds began to secede to the Sith invasion fleet voluntarily, either out of fear or because they believed that the corrupt and ineffectual Republic was finally about to fall. However, the Republic armadas were saved from certain destruction by the talents of a young [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] named [[Bastila Shan]]. During a long string of Republic losses, her skills in battle meditation staved off utter defeat, and when the Sith were on the brink of victory, Bastila led a Jedi strike team to invade [[Darth Revan's flagship]]. Ever ambitious, Malak fired upon his master's vessel, hoping to destroy his enemies and usurp control of the Sith Empire with one swift stroke, but all did not go as he had planned. The ship was destroyed, but the Jedi were able to escape with a critically injured Revan. The Jedi Council repaired Revan's broken mind, implanting him with the personality of a loyal soldier of the Republic. As he fought the Sith Empire alongside Bastila, he regained memories of being the Sith Lord Revan, but stayed loyal to the Republic and to the light side of the Force. He led the assault on the Star Forge during the [[Battle of Rakata Prime]] and killed his former pupil. The Star Forge plunged into Rakata's sun and was destroyed, effectively destroying the Sith Empire of Revan and Malak as well.<ref name="KOTOR" />

===The Sith Triumvirate's Sith Empire===
{{Main|Sith Triumvirate}}
[[File:Kreia_Trayus_Hoodless.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Darth Traya, Sith Lord of Betrayal]]
{{Quote|To be united by hatred is a&hellip; fragile alliance at best.|Darth Traya|audio=KreiaFragileAlliance.flac|<ref name="KotOR2" />}}
The [[Sith Triumvirate]] was a loose alliance of what remained of Darth Revan's Sith. It was solidified sometime after the Battle of Rakata Prime around the Trayus Academy on Malachor V. This organization was made up of several, if not hundreds, of [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentices]], [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Masters]], and, most importantly, [[Sith assassin/Legends|Sith assassins]], and fell under the leadership of three powerful Sith Lords, [[Kreia|Darth Traya]], [[Darth Nihilus]], and [[Darth Sion]], co-rulers of a new Sith Empire. From Malachor V, they subtly intervened with galactic affairs, using Darth Traya's idea of echoes in the Force, and corrupting Jedi to the dark side. Sion quickly grew impatient of waiting to fight the Jedi and the Republic, while Nihilus grew hungry and needed Force sustenance.<ref name="KotOR2" />

The two conspired against Darth Traya and attacked when she was vulnerable. The two Lords used an unknown Force technique to sever her connection to the Force, leaving her cast out by both Jedi and Sith. Abandoning her Sith name and title and traveling as Kreia, the fallen Sith Lord directed her anger towards the Force itself, viewing it as a malevolent intelligent being. She directed her manipulations toward [[Meetra Surik]], who had cut herself off from the Force following the events of the Mandalorian Wars, and in whom Kreia saw a means to destroy the Force itself. Sion and Nihilus went their separate ways, Sion carrying out a [[First Jedi Purge|purge]] of the Jedi Order and Nihilus [[Conclave at Katarr|consuming entire civilizations]] in his hunger.<ref name="KotOR2" />

Under Kreia's direction, Surik retrained herself as a Jedi and fought the Sith Empire of Sion and Nihilus, eventually destroying them both. Kreia revealed her true intentions, killing the survivors of the Jedi High Council and luring the Jedi Exile to the Trayus Academy on Malachor V. There, Kreia&mdash;once again in the guise of Darth Traya, Sith Lord of Betrayal&mdash;fought Surik with the intention of using the retrained Jedi's unique connection to the Force in order to destroy the Force entirely. Surik defeated Traya and Malachor V was destroyed by [[Bao-Dur]]'s [[Mass Shadow Generator/Legends|Mass Shadow Generator]] in [[3951 BBY]], ending her Sith Empire once and for all.<ref name="KotOR2" />

===The revitalized Sith Empire===
{{Main|Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)}}
[[File:Sith_Emperor.jpg|thumb|right|150px|The Sith Emperor plotted for generations before returning to the known galaxy in force.]]
{{Quote|Our time has come. For three hundred years, we prepared. We grew stronger. While you rested in your cradle of power, believing your people were safe and protected. You were trusted to lead the Republic but you were deceived, as our powers of the Dark Side have blinded you. You assumed no force could challenge you and now&hellip; finally, we have returned.|Sith Lord Darth Malgus during the Sacking of Coruscant|audio=SithEmpireReEmergence.flac|<ref name="TOR" />}}
In the aftermath of the Great Hyperspace War of 5000 BBY, survivors of the original Sith Empire established a new Sith Empire in the galaxy's Unknown Regions. This empire,<ref name="Revan" /> also known as the "True Sith,"<ref name="KotOR2" /> was led by the [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor]], a surviving Sith Lord of the old Sith Empire. The refugees [[Sith exodus|wandered]] aimlessly through space in search of a new home. [[4980 BBY|Twenty years]] after their departure from the original Empire's [[Sith Worlds/Legends|territory]], the Sith discovered the forgotten world of Dromund Kaas and settled it to begin the process of rebuilding. It was this Sith Empire<ref name="Revan" /> which offered the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Neo-Crusaders]] their new crusade against their common foe, resulting in the [[Mandalorian Wars]].<ref name="Sith">"''The Sith came to us with an offer&mdash;to fight a worthy enemy in a battle that would be remembered forever.''" &mdash;[[Canderous Ordo]]<sup>[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]</sup></ref>

During the war, Revan [[Mission to Dromund Kaas|discovered]] and was turned by the Emperor before invading the Republic at the head of his own Sith Empire.<ref name="Revan" /> Around three hundred years after the [[Jedi Civil War]], the Sith Empire&mdash;still under the command of the Emperor, his life extended through Sith sorcery&mdash;invaded the Republic, sparking the [[Great Galactic War]]. In [[3653 BBY]], the [[Treaty of Coruscant]] ended the Great Galactic War, giving way to the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], the galaxy divided between the Sith Empire and the Galactic Republic.<ref name="TOR" />

===Darth Sidious' Galactic Empire===
{{Main|Galactic Empire/Legends}}
{{Quote|We are an Empire ruled by the ''majority''! An Empire ruled by a new Constitution! An Empire of ''laws'', not of politicians! An Empire devoted to the preservation of a just society. Of a ''safe'' and ''secure'' society! We are an Empire that will stand for ''ten thousand years''!|Palpatine|<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (novelization)">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref>}}
[[File:EmperorPalpatine-TCGCoreSet.png|thumb|right|240px|Darth Sidious destroyed the Galactic Republic from within, transforming it into the Galactic Empire.]]
The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] can be said to have begun with the scheming aspiration of Senator [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], whose alter ego was the Sith Lord Darth Sidious. Using the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] as a pawn to [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|blockade Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], he used manipulation of the crisis, as well as of [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], to instigate a [[Vote of No Confidence/Legends|Vote of No Confidence]] in Supreme Chancellor [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]], and ultimately to become Chancellor himself. When his apprentice, [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], was defeated by Jedi Knight [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] on Naboo,<ref name="Episode I">{{Film|I}}</ref> Sidious took on the former Jedi [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] as his new apprentice. Count Dooku then joined with the Trade Federation under [[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] and others to form the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. This group, known as the Separatists, ignited a war with the Galactic Republic known as the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. It was named after the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] used by the Republic.<ref name="Episode II">{{Film|II}}</ref>

Manipulating the war from behind the scenes, Palpatine arranged for [[Emergency Powers Act/Legends|extraordinary powers]] to be granted to the office of Supreme Chancellor, and for the deaths of many Jedi throughout the war.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (novelization)" /> However, Jedi Knight [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] discovered that Palpatine was a Sith Lord and, after informing Jedi Master [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] of his discovery, a Jedi task force, led by Windu himself, attempted to arrest him. After a [[Showdown on Coruscant|brief duel]], Palpatine appeared to be defeated. Skywalker arrived and demanded Windu not kill the Sith Lord. Deeply troubled, Skywalker nonetheless helped Palpatine kill Windu, and thus became the Emperor's new apprentice, Darth Vader. Palpatine then proceeded to carry out the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], which eliminated almost all of the thousands of Jedi, and had Vader eliminate Nute Gunray and the other Separatist leaders on the fiery world of [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]], thus bringing an end to the Clone Wars. Secure in his power and position, Palpatine used the so-called Jedi rebellion to issue the [[Imperialization/Legends|Declaration of a New Order]] and declared himself Emperor in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="Episode III">{{Film|III}}</ref>

The Galactic Empire flourished under Palpatine's rule until the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], also known as the Rebel Alliance, became a serious threat following the [[Corellian Treaty]] and the issuance of the [[Declaration of Rebellion/Legends|Declaration of Rebellion]] in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]].<ref name="TFU">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref> The Rebel Alliance engaged in guerrilla warfare against the Empire, and scored a major victory against the Galactic Empire at the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], where hero, Jedi apprentice of Kenobi, and son of Vader, Luke Skywalker destroyed the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first]] [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]].<ref name="Episode IV">{{Film|IV}}</ref> Skywalker continued to fight the Galactic Empire, and continued his training under Jedi Master [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]].<ref name="Episode V">{{Film|V}}</ref> Four years later, the Rebel Alliance destroyed the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], resulting in the deaths of Palpatine and Vader, the end of the Rule of Two,<ref name="Episode VI">{{Film|VI}}</ref> and the fracturing of the Galactic Empire. The Rebel Alliance reestablished itself as the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="Heir">''[[Heir to the Empire]]''</ref>

The remnant of the Galactic Empire and Palpatine's Sith threatened the galaxy in the following decades in various resurgent forms, such as the Imperial [[Warlord/Legends|Warlords]] who engaged in [[Imperial Civil War|inter-imperial war]] even as they opposed the New Republic,<ref name="Dark Empire">[[Dark Empire 1|''Dark Empire'' 1]]</ref> a [[Dark Empire|reunited Empire]] led by a [[Essence transfer|possessed]] [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] of Palpatine,<ref name="Dark Empire 2">[[Dark Empire 2|''Dark Empire'' 2]]</ref> the military [[Thrawn campaign|campaigns]] of [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]], and the machinations of Palpatine's former Sith Acolytes, such as the [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hands]]<ref name="Heir" /> and other [[Dark side adept/Legends|Dark Side Adepts]]<ref name="TGODV">''[[The Glove of Darth Vader]]''</ref> or the [[Second Imperium]].<ref name="YJK">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Shadow Academy]]''</ref> The New Republic, now called the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]], almost returned to the practices of Palpatine's Empire during the [[Second Galactic Civil War]] with the [[Confederation]]<ref name="Betrayal">''[[Legacy of the Force: Betrayal]]''</ref> under the guidance of [[Darth Caedus]], the apprentice of [[Lumiya]], the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lady of the Sith]].<ref name="Inferno">''[[Legacy of the Force: Inferno]]''</ref> The [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] would eventually unify with the Galactic Alliance, and [[Jagged Fel]] would become Emperor of the Empire, establishing the Fel Empire. The Fel Empire turned away from the teachings of the Sith, and actively opposed Darth Krayt's One Sith after the [[Sith–Imperial War]] in [[127 ABY]].<ref name="Legacy 0.5">[[Star Wars: Legacy (2006) 0½|''Star Wars: Legacy'' (2006) 0½]]</ref>

===Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire===
{{Main|Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire}}
[[File:KraytWyyrlok_Badass.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Darth Krayt and his regent, Darth Wyyrlok]]
{{Quote|Roan Fel never really embraced the war or the idea of a unified galaxy. He went along with it as a political necessity. That's not what the Empire&mdash;what the galaxy&mdash;needs. The galaxy writhes in chaos and disorder. It requires a man of vision. I am that man of vision. I am the new Emperor.|Darth Krayt|<ref name="Broken 1">[[Legacy (2006) 1|''Legacy'' (2006) 1]]</ref>}}
Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire was the government that formed out of the Fel Empire in [[130 ABY]], when Darth Krayt, Dark Lord of the Sith, made a coup against Emperor [[Roan Fel]]. When the [[Council of Moffs/Legends|Moff Council]] invoked the [[Treaty of Anaxes]] against the will of Emperor Roan Fel, and in 127 ABY, the Sith-Imperial War broke out, and the One Sith allied with the Empire. The war resulted in the fall of the Alliance and the reestablishment of the Empire as the primary galactic government. The territories and bureaucracy of the Alliance were absorbed into the Empire, but the [[Core Fleet|Galactic Alliance Core Fleet]] refused to surrender, and continued to fight the resurgent Empire.<ref name="Legacy 0">[[Star Wars: Legacy (2006) 0|''Star Wars: Legacy'' (2006) 0]]</ref> Shortly after the fall of the Alliance, the Emperor called upon the entire New Jedi Order to surrender and subject their will to the Empire, in which some of them did, becoming [[Imperial Knight]]s, while the others remained to the will of the Force and retreated to Ossus.<ref name="Legacy 8">[[Legacy (2006) 8|''Legacy'' (2006) 8]]</ref> After the Alliance defeat and the [[Massacre at Ossus]], the Sith under the command of Darth Krayt turned against Emperor Fel. He launched a daring coup, marching with his cohorts straight into Fel's audience chamber himself, and killing [[Roan Fel's double|the man who sat on the throne]].<ref name="Broken 1" /> Fel eluded the Sith forces for [[137 ABY|seven years]], then resurfaced on [[Bastion/Legends|Bastion]], seizing control of the military forces there and inciting the [[Second Imperial Civil War]].<ref name="Legacy Era Campaign Guide">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

==Government and politics==
[[File:LudoVsSadow.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Ludo Kressh duels Naga Sadow before Marka Ragnos for rights to the title of Dark Lord of the Sith.]]
{{Quote|They must be precursors to an invasion&hellip;we should kill them at once!" <br /> "No&mdash;not until we interrogate them. They may be alien spies&hellip;or they may be the key to ripe new fields for the Sith Lords to conquer.|Ludo Kressh and Naga Sadow discuss the Daragons|<ref name="TOTJ 2" />}}
Much of the structure of the Empire had changed following 6,900 BBY due to the arrival of the Dark Jedi Exiles. Their government evolved into a feudal system, led by a cabal of [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] who owed allegiance to a single Dark Lord of the Sith. It was these individuals that controlled the now Force-using magocracy of the Sith Empire. Politics amongst the ambitious, power-hungry Sith Lords was naturally divisive, and infighting between rivals was common. The empire's only hope for stability rested on a powerful Dark Lord who could control his subordinates.<ref name="TEA" /> 

The title of Dark Lord of the Sith was typically given to the individual by their deceased predecessor who manifested as a Dark Side Spirit after being interred within their tomb.<ref name="DSS" /> The cabal beneath him were the [[Sith Council]] who were a body of advisors to the reigning Dark Lord of the Sith. It consisted of ten members made up of Sith Lords within the Empire. Each Lord on the Council personally ruled over a dozen worlds. This Council convened in a [[Sith Citadel (Ziost)|great citadel]] on Ziost. In this ancient age, the Lords of the Sith Empire were the undisputed masters of the worlds that fell under their control.<ref name="FFCA" />

Political factions were also known to exist within the ranks of the government of the Sith Empire with such [[Ludo Kressh's faction|coalitions]] formed around specific Sith Lords.<ref name="TOTJ 3" />

==Society and culture==
[[File:Massassi-JATM.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A Kissai and Massassi]]
{{Quote|Evil began in a time before recorded history, when magicians made themselves into kings&hellip; and gods&hellip; using the power of the dark side of the Force. The weak minded have ever been ready to obey one who wields great power. Those who learned the power of the darkside were quick to exploit this weakness -- to make war. Again and again, the dark side has surged forth, like a storm&hellip; devouring whole worlds and entire star systems. Those who mastered dark power ''became'' the dark power. They unleashed destruction, for no other reason than selfish gain. They despoiled nations&hellip; destroyed whole civilizations. Some of them, I am ashamed to say, were Jedi.|Jedi Master Ood Bnar|<ref name="saga5">[[Tales of the Jedi 5|''Tales of the Jedi'' 5]]</ref>}}
Culturally, the Sith Empire was very different from that of the Republic, being much more ecumenically-driven than its counterpart. The Sith Empire was hierarchical, utilizing both a rigid caste system and a stratified rank structure to put its subjects in their proper place. Due to the length of time over which the Sith were divided into castes<ref name="BoS" /> (across approximately 100,000 years),<ref name="END" /> each caste was sometimes referred to as a sub-species of Sith. The [[Kissai]] were the priest caste of the Sith who served as spiritual leaders that indoctrinated others into Sith teachings.<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide" /> In contrast, the ferocious [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] were the warrior caste of the Sith. They were unswervingly obedient to the Sith Lords they served, though they technically owed loyalty to the Dark Lord of the Sith. The [[Zuguruk]] were engineer caste of the Sith, a clever, nimble lot, responsible for building and maintaining Sith technology, including droids and starships. The meek and servile [[Grotthu]] Sith slaves were the lowliest caste of the Sith. They were often used as sacrifices. The Sith Lords used them for slave labor and menial tasks,<ref name="BoS" /> such as [[Ludo Kressh's pedicure set|grooming their feet]].<ref name="LotSPa" /> Most citizens of the Empire lived in this meager caste-driven structure where they toiled to serve their masters' ambitions or died by the millions in internecine warfare. They were ultimately governed by a militaristic culture with a great reverence for the dead.<ref name="TEA" /> When a Sith Lord died, his slaves were buried alive with his body in his tomb on Korriban.<ref name="TOTJ 2" /> 

When Adas unified the Sith nations, he took the title of ''"Sith'ari"'' which, when translated, meant "Sith Overlord" in Basic. Following the death of Adas, many claimed the title of Sith'ari and fought each other in a civil war.<ref name="END" /> By 6,900 BBY, the word "Sith'ari" took on the approximate meaning "Chosen One", referring to an unidentified individual who would fulfill a particular Sith prophecy,<ref name="BoS" /> this prophecy was later fulfilled by Darth Bane.<ref name="TCSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

[[File:Massassi_and_Kissai.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Members of the Sith species.]]
The term ''"Jen'ari"'' was the title translated "Dark Lord of the Sith" in Basic. Jen'ari were the greatest and most powerful of the Sith Lords who took the place of the Sith King in the Sith hierarchy.<ref name="END" /> There was only one Dark Lord of the Sith at a time,<ref name="dlots1">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 1|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 1]]</ref> who was the head of the Sith Council, and ruler of the Sith Empire.<ref name="TOTJ 3" /> The first Dark Lord, [[Ajunta Pall]], was the leader of the Exiles;<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide" /> later Dark Lords were Sith Lords who assumed the title after the death of the previous Dark Lord, defeating any rival claimant to the title in combat (often resulting in death, or at least disfigurement).<ref name="TOTJ 3" /> From 6,900 BBY to 5,000 BBY,<ref name="NEC" /> the Sith Lords collectively ruled the Empire through a governing body known as the Sith Council, which the Dark Lord ruled over and commanded;<ref name="TOTJ 3" /> each member of the Council had a personal fleet.<ref name="TOTJ 4" /> Many Dark Lords had partial Exile ancestry, which was, in some, considered more desirable.<ref name="TOTJ 2" /> After the Sith Emperor reconstituted the Sith Empire, all 12 members of the [[Dark Council]] used the title "Dark Lord of the Sith", although it is uncertain if the title "Jen'ari" remained in use in any capacity, or was abandoned for the title "[[Darth/Legends|Darth]]."<ref name="TOR" />

Before the formation of the Sith Empire, the Sith were engaged in constant warfare with one another, though this was seen as an acceptable practice as they believed it to be a fundamental aspect of their existence. This meant that they lived both a barbaric yet strangely harmonious existence on their homeworld. The early Sith often engaged in sentient sacrifices which they made to their deities.<ref name="END" /> Their constant warring led to a dwindling of the population on their original homeworld of Korriban as well as cultivated an intensely xenophobic society.<ref name="JATM" /> After the arrival of the Exiles, only those that were Force-sensitive had the capacity to reach the upper echlons of the Sith Empire. Those that were blind to the Force were considered useless; fit for only common labor purposes or simple bureaucratic work. Amongst the elite, power was craved due to the intense feelings of greed perpetrated by the dark side which also meant that these individuals were also ambitious as well as paranoid. This society encouraged the survival of the fittest with only the most ruthless and powerful rising to positions of power as well as surviving.<ref name="DSS" />

This empire ultimately thrived on slavery as well as exploitation and oppression of the masses. In addition, they lived in constant belief that they would face external threats to their dominion and thus had a belief in expansion or dying. Some believed that this was a necessity for the Sith as they hungered for new lands and riches to bring under their control. This allowed for Naga Sadow to lead his forces during the Great Hyperspace War though despite this being the case, there were other traditional and more conservative factions that believed in remaining within their territory in order to preserve their ways.<ref name="TJ:TFSE:2">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 2]]</ref>

During the time of the first Sith Empire, there were many instances of travelers stumbling into Sith space where they became slaves to one of the many members of the nobility. Over the years of enslavement, these aliens and outsiders continued to live for generations whereupon they forgot their origins thus turning them into true subjects of the Sith. Some Sith Lords even found value in the descendants of these foreigners such as those of the Tapani worlds due to their skills in science. Natural born Sith tended to focus on sorcery while the Tapani's excellence in the fields of science meant that they became valued members of the Empire and developed the industrial as well as medical infrastructure for several Sith Lords. Through such means as those presented by the Tapani, the Sith developed new lightsaber construction techniques that were more advanced than those produced by either Sith or Jedi. However, the intense rivalry and fierce competitive nature of Sith society meant that ranking Sith Lords never shared these new developments or weapons. Among the Sith, about glorification of self and the subjugation of others was a constant aspect within their society.<ref name="LotSPa" />

[[File:Sith_species.jpg|thumb|left|right|200px|The five castes of the Sith Empire (top to bottom): Sith Lord, Kissai, Zuguruk, Massassi, Grotthu.]]
One of the greatest secrets of the ancient Sith was their devotion to the arts of Sith sorcery. As such, those individuals that practiced this art took on the title of Sith mages who held great mystical power that allowed them to cause stars to go supernova.<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide" /> The original Sith were also quite skilled in the art of [[Sith alchemy]] though it was the Dark Jedi Exiles who later became Sith Lords that perfected the ability.<ref name="JvSTEGF" /> Originally, the species wasn't a united people, instead preferring to stay within different tribes. These were led by one or more sorcerers who were in charge with the groups protection. This remained the case until the arrival of the Exiles who took interest in the species' techniques in drawing on the power of the dark side of the Force which they used to accomplish their sorcery.<ref name="TJC" /> This practice was used by pure blood Sith who often dwelled in [[Library-temple]]s where they sat in meditation as well as recorded their experiences as well as experiments.<ref name="ATDS" /> They also created many tools designed to enhance or project their power which was commonly seen in Sith talismans. These dark side empowered constructs were capable of a wide range of feats from being simple concentration tools to being a trap that turned other Force users to the dark side when being used or defensive tools that absorbed weapon fire and even being used for healing.<ref name="TJC" /> They also created special chambers and sanctuaries that amplified the power of the Force which were either used as [[Meditation chamber/Legends|Meditation chamber]] or [[Focusing chamber]]s.<ref name="TSC" /> One of the greater feats was the capacity to create sentient vessels such as Meditation Spheres that were capable of enhancing the power of a Sith sorcerer.<ref name="sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref>

The Sith Empire had also made use of droids and recognized their potential as security troops leading to several different designs to be produced. Schematics for these droids were often stored within holocrons and though their inner workings were inferior to later generation droids, the fact that Sith alchemy was used in their construction meant that their outer plating was equal to a low powered shield generator.<ref name="TSC" />

==Military==
[[File:Massassi_at_the_funeral_of_Marka_Ragnos.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Massassi warriors of the Sith Empire]]
The [[Navy/Legends|navy]] of the Sith Empire included [[Starship/Legends|starships]] of many different types. These included [[Frigate/Legends|frigates]], such as the [[Derriphan-class battleship|''Derriphan''-class battleship]],<ref name="TOTJ 4" /> smaller attack craft such as the [[Blade-class starfighter|Blade starfighter]],<ref name="LotSPr" /> [[Sith drop ship]], [[Sith escort gunship]], and [[Sith starfighter]], as well as non-combat craft such as the [[Sith dreadnaught|Sith personnel carrier]],<ref name="TSC" /> and the [[Shuttle/Legends|Sith shuttle]].<ref name="fall3">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 3|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 3]]</ref> The Sith also crafted [[Sentience/Legends|semi-sentient]] spaceships called [[Sith Meditation Sphere]]s that were capable of independent action, even the training of apprentices.<ref name="sacrifice" />

The Sith Empire's ground forces largely consisted of Massassi warriors that served as shock troopers and brutal weapons of terror on the battlefield that were led by ranking Sith Lords.<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide" /> Massassi warriors, armed with [[Sith sword]]s such as the [[lanvarok]] or [[Sith war sword|war swords]], often served as foot soldiers in the campaigns of the Sith and also piloted the great warships of the empire. In battle, they fought with a single minded fury and selflessly hurled themselves in combat against their foes.<ref name="DSS" /> Early in their history, the Sith Empire came to realize the potential in the use of automated droids to enhance the combat performances of their military. Droids such as [[Sith Elite Warbot|elite warbots]], [[Sith Slayer droid|slayer droids]], and [[Sith Sentry|sentries]] were often treated with alchemy in order to improve their construction materials and add to their combat capabilities. As such, several different forms of droids were manufactured which ranged from simple security droids to elite warbots to fully fledged war droids.<ref name="TSC" />

In addition, they also made use of many different forms of creatures&mdash;such as [[Chrysalide]], [[Sith war behemoth]]s, [[Sith warbird]]s, [[Sith war rhino]]s, [[Sith war worm]]s, and [[Silooth/Legends|Silooth]]&mdash;that augmented the fighting power of their legions.<ref name="SWBa">{{Wizards|url=starwars/article.asp?x=sw20010809d_behemoth&c=rpg|series=Creature Feature|text=Sith War Behemoth}}</ref> These domesticated creatures were often used as mounts for heavy weaponry and artillery.<ref name="TSC" /> These beasts were often treated with Sith alchemy and were part of centuries long breeding programs that were designed to create easily trained animals that responded to certain commands. To enforce control over these creatures, the Sith often used standard command coding in order to manage these animals in combat engagements. This combined with generations of breeding meant that anyone trained in animal handling skills were capable of controlling certain Sith war beasts. When ready for war, these creatures often accompanied the Sith army where they were outfitted with gun turrets as well as other weaponry to add to their terrifying potential on the battlefield.<ref name="SWBa" />

==Astrography==
[[File:SithSpace.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The worlds of the first Sith Empire in Sith Space]]
{{Quote|You wish to know about the worlds of the Sith Empire? There were many, well over one hundred that were habitable, and the Sith controlled the riches of a thousand species.|Seviss Vaa of the Brotherhood of Darkness|<ref name="JvSTEGF" />}}
The portion of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] that the Sith Empire ruled was known as [[Sith Worlds/Legends|Sith Space]] in a region of space surrounded by the [[Stygian Caldera]]. It contained at least 120 inhabited worlds,<ref name="JvSTEGF" /> including some early Sith colonies outside of Sith Space, such as [[Arbra/Legends|Arbra]], [[Malachor V]], [[Tund/Legends|Tund]], and [[Arkania/Legends|Arkania]]. Worlds of special note in Sith Space were the capital planet of [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]] and the graveyard planet of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], which was placed along the [[Daragon Trail]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|route]] to the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]]. Travel between Sith Space and the Republic was known to be rare as the Sith were more concerned with making war against one another or cowing other civilizations within the interstellar neighbourhood.<ref name="TEA" />

Along the [[Kamat Krote]] route were the planets of [[Bosthirda/Legends|Bosthirda]], Dromund Kaas, and [[Jaguada/Legends|Jaguada]]. Jaguada was also included in the [[Kamat Aegit]] route along with [[Begeren]], Kalsunor, Ashas Ree, and [[Khar Delba]]. [[Nicht Ka system/Legends|Nicht Ka]] was along the [[Nache Bhelfia]] route that connected Korriban to Ziost, and the Zorfee Trete route connected [[Ch'hodos]] to Ashas Ree. The [[Descri Wris]] route connected [[Korriz]], [[Athiss/Legends|Athiss]], Svolten, Bhargebba, and [[Nfolgai]]. [[Krayiss II]] and [[Rhelg/Legends|Rhelg]] were on the far side of the Nache Bhelfia route across from Nicht Ka. Thule, the [[Iliabath system/Legends|Iliabath system]], and [[Corbos]] were outside the Stygian Caldera.<ref name="TEA" />

When the Sith Empire fell, refugees fled back to the worlds of Ambria, Kesh, Thule, Tund, Vjun, Yavin 4, and into the Unknown Regions.<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
When the [[canon]] was that the Exiles' Sith Empire was created ~[[25,000 BBY/Legends|25,000 BBY]],''<ref name="NEGC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref>'' it was assumed that the Exiles' Sith Empire was responsible for Sith activity before 6900 BBY such as the "Sith-backed uprisings" that led to [[Republic Fleet Systems]] being founded ~[[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000 BBY]],<ref name="EGVV">''[[The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref> the Sith spirits that had been in the library-temple on Krayiss II since 14,000 BBY,<ref name="ATDS" /> Dathka Graush reigning in 7000 BBY,<ref name="POLS">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20031002korriban1|series=Korriban: Planet of Lost Souls|text=Part 1: Haunted Hideout}}</ref>, and the Sith Library of [[Veeshas Tuwan]] being established in 7000 BBY,<ref name="EGAS" /> but when the creation of the Exiles' Sith Empire was [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] to have happened in [[6900 BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> the implication became that Adas's Sith Empire was responsible for all Sith activity prior to 6900 BBY.
